exposure: Sera from normotensive pregnant women (control sera)
Depleted control sera supplemented with peEVs (placenta-derived extracellular vesicles from PE women)
PE-NETs (neutrophil extracellular traps obtained after incubation with PE sera)
cohort: Sera were collected from preeclamptic and normotensive pregnant women, and neutrophils were obtained from donors, for use in *in vitro* experiments on microvascular endothelial cells.
finding: Both circulating extracellular vesicles (EVs) and neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) from preeclamptic pregnant women deleteriously affect endothelial cells, with EVs triggering a pro-oxidant and proinflammatory state, and NETs potentiating complement system activation.
